summary: It's a Wonderful World is a card-drafting engine-builder where you draft from a hand, then simultaneously decide which cards to recycle for resources versus construct for ongoing production and points. The tense part is that production resolves in a fixed resource order each round, so timing your engine and covering shortfalls (or converting excess via recycling) is the core puzzle.
praised: Efficient simultaneous-play drafting means little downtime despite being a drafting game
Satisfying engine-building puzzle with meaningful tension between recycling now vs building for later
Attractive production and thematic sci-fi/civilization art
Scales well and plays quickly for the amount of decision-making involved
criticised: Can feel like a multiplayer solitaire with limited direct interaction beyond drafting
Some randomness in what cards appear can swing a game
Rules around production order and resource conversion have a learning curve for new players
Later plays can feel a bit samey without expansions

interaction.kind: drafting against opponents but mostly parallel engine-building

scoring.why: Points come from multiple card types (empire cards, achievements, bonuses) so the winner is whoever builds the most efficient, well-timed production engine
